method.question: Can the high profile be made to beat lean, and lean + the 0.6B reranker, on a set large enough to resolve the difference?
method.corpora: Three live corpora read in place and copied to a temp project per run (nothing written beside them): hippo's own (108 indexed memories), a second project's (110) and a third's (1,070). User and private tiers off. One embedder per process; MLX's buffer cache capped at 512 MB (embed_mlx.cap_mlx_cache).
method.sampling: 350 memories drawn at random (seed 20261126) from files with frontmatter, at least 400 characters, not superseded or invalidated: 60 / 80 / 210 by corpus. 3 were index files and were skipped: 347 questions (60 / 80 / 207).
method.questions: One question per sampled memory, written by a language model (Claude, seven independent writers of 50 memories each) that was shown ONLY that memory's file: no retriever, no search, no other memory. So no question is derived from what lean (or anything else) retrieves. Each is an 8-30 word message a developer might type to a coding agent, a question or a task message. Alternating by sample order, half are 'natural' (the memory's own key terms may appear) and half 'paraphrase' (the distinctive words of the memory's name and description avoided), reported separately because natural wording favors the lexical lane and paraphrase the dense one.
method.known_bias: Writers read roughly the first 1,300-2,200 characters of each file, so questions lean on a memory's description and opening section rather than its tail. Every memory is the target of at most one question; multi-hop, temporal, update and abstention questions are not in this set. Plain recall() top 10 is scored: the prompt hook's gate and count rule are not exercised, and no off-topic probe is included, so nothing here measures abstention or what a lower floor would inject on prompts that deserve nothing.
method.labels: Start: the memory a question was written from is its one right answer. Check: pooled judging. For every question the union of the top 3 of eight arms (lean, BM25 alone, lean + reranker over 30, high, high + reranker over 30, high with whole-memory rows, and the lean and high dense lanes alone) plus the source memory, shuffled, each shown as the first 650 characters of its file, went to a second set of ten language-model judges who did not know which candidate was the source or which arm returned it (3,617 candidates). They confirmed the source memory for 342 of 347 questions and accepted 41 other memories as also correct across 35 questions; those 41 count as right answers in every number here. The 5 unconfirmed sources were kept as right answers. Arms added after the judging (the p2/ arms and the 8B) were not in the pool, so a correct memory only they surface is not credited: a small bias against them.
method.tiers: lane/ arms rank by one dense lane alone (cosine, no floor, no fusion): description rows, and with '+chunks' the body-chunk rows max-pooled onto their memory. pipe/ and p2/ arms are recall() itself as the warm server serves it. Rerank arms score the top `pool` fused hits with Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B and cut to 10.
method.document_variants: shipped = the description row ('name words. description') plus up to 3 body chunks from the first 1,500 characters. desc+body = the description row replaced by description + body. whole = the description row replaced by the whole file. Both cut at the embedder's 1,024 tokens (lean's model cuts at 512). desc-only and /no-chunks zero the body-chunk rows.
method.latency: In-process, models loaded, one query at a time, on the owner's 128 GB M4 Max while other work ran (load average stamped per run); the first two 4B corpora ran alone, later runs shared the machine with the label judging. Read latencies as load-stamped, quality as the evidence.
method.set_fingerprint: sha256 64391ccc04f98e2d over the sorted corpus::stem::query lines of the private question file; the file itself is kept outside the repository
method.reproducibility: bench/high_eval_set.py is the builder (sample, pool, gold). The corpora are live and moved during the run day (one gained two eligible memories), so re-running `sample` today draws a different set; the set measured here is fixed by its private files and the fingerprint above, not by the seed alone.

note: private corpora and questions: counts and intervals only, no query and no memory name. Intervals are 95%: Wilson for a hit rate, percentile bootstrap (2000 resamples, seed 20261126) for MRR and for every paired difference.
corpus_labels: hippo = hippo's own corpus (HCR-6's); corpus-b and corpus-c are two private project corpora of 110 and 1,070 indexed memories
summary: Set: 347 held-out questions over three corpora, written from one memory each with no retriever in the loop; labels checked by blind pooled judging (342 of 347 source memories confirmed, 41 more correct memories credited). Every interval is 95%.
high as shipped (4B) beats lean: 303 vs 286 of 347 in the top 10 (paired +0.049 [+0.012, +0.089]), MRR 0.712 vs 0.668 (+0.044 [+0.009, +0.083]). HCR-6's 38 rows could not resolve this.

The query instruction, the dense floor and the dense/lexical fusion weight move nothing outside their intervals, on either model, in recall(). Instruction 'none' is 2.5x faster to embed (57 vs 144 ms p50) at no measured cost.

The document text is the largest lever. Embedding each memory's whole file (to the model's token cut) in place of its description row: 4B high 303 -> 320 hits; the same change on lean (bge-small, 512-token cut) 286 -> 307. On the two smaller corpora lean with whole-memory rows is within the interval of high with them; on all three high still leads (+0.037 [+0.003, +0.072] hits, +0.046 [+0.014, +0.077] MRR).

MMR (RCL-4's diversity re-cut, lambda 0.8) costs hits on this set: off, lean 286 -> 302 (+0.046 [+0.020, +0.075]) and 4B high with whole-memory rows 320 -> 335 (+0.043 [+0.017, +0.069]). Graph expansion matters here mainly by exempting linked memories from MMR: with MMR off, turning the graph off changes nothing (identical top 10s on both models). This set has one target per question, so it cannot score what MMR is for (diversity across near-duplicates); see the caveats.

Best configuration measured: 4B high, whole-memory rows, MMR off: 335 of 347 (96.5%), MRR 0.777, 127 ms p50. Against lean + the 0.6B reranker over 30 (306, MRR 0.757, 1,067 ms p50): +0.084 [+0.046, +0.118] hits, MRR +0.020 [-0.018, +0.056] (not resolved), at an eighth of the latency and 3.9 GB more resident memory.

The reranker adds nothing resolved on top of whole-memory rows: high, whole rows, reranker over 30 (MMR on) reads 325 hits, MRR 0.779 against 320 / 0.754 without it (+0.014 [-0.017, +0.046] hits, +0.025 [-0.014, +0.063] MRR), and 10 fewer hits than the best configuration (-0.029 [-0.058, -0.003]) for ~1 s more per recall.

The 8B ties the 4B everywhere recall() serves: shipped 305 vs 303 (+0.006 [-0.026, +0.035]), with the reranker 321 vs 320, best configuration on two corpora 134 vs 134. Its dense lane alone is better on whole-memory rows (+0.045 [+0.008, +0.085] MRR on 140 questions), which fusion does not carry through. It costs 7.27 GB resident against 3.86 and ~200 vs ~127 ms per recall.

lean + reranker inside SERVE_BUDGET_MS (1,500 ms): pool 20 keeps pool 30's quality within its interval (300 vs 305 hits, MRR -0.012 [-0.029, +0.002]) at 785 / 1,002 ms rerank p50 / p95 on a loaded machine. Cutting passages to 80 or 160 characters loses MRR (-0.163, -0.059, both resolved). Slice size: 1,024-token slices are ~6% faster than the shipped 2,048; larger slices are slower. A shared-prefix KV cache matches quality but is slower at p95.
All gains are on paraphrased questions: with the memory's own terms in the question every arm finds 96-99%; without them lean finds 118 of 173 and the best high configuration 162.
caveats: Questions and judgments are a language model's, not developers'; writers read each memory's opening ~1,300-2,200 characters, which favors description-heavy rows less than whole-memory rows would suggest but is still a bias toward the head of each file.

One target per question, no multi-hop, temporal, update or abstention rows, and no off-topic probes: nothing here measures abstention, injection volume on prompts that deserve nothing, or the diversity MMR exists to provide. Turning MMR off, or re-embedding with whole-memory rows, changes the cosine distribution HCR-3 calibrated the 4B's floor, gate and count rule on; those need re-running before either ships.
Plain recall() top 10 is scored, not the prompt hook (its gate and count rule, the floor-collapsed rows HCR-3 traced).
The 8B's whole-memory arms ran on two corpora (140 questions), not the 1,070-memory one. Arms added after judging were not in the judging pool, a small bias against them.
Latencies are in-process, one query at a time, load-stamped per run (load average 1.1 to 29.7); quality is the evidence.
mxfp8 against a higher-precision 4B was not run: no bf16 conversion is on disk and the download (~8 GB) needs the owner's word.

The bench process's own footprint (11-19 GB) holds several copies of the dense matrix for the variants; it is not what a warm server holds. The embedder's resident memory is the per-server cost: 3.86 GB (4B), 7.27 GB (8B), with MLX peaks of 5.4 and 8.8 GB under the 512 MB cache cap.
